summary: George Berrington closed the programme with Simon Clarke and Priya Natarajan by modelling the economics of each service line. DD runs at lower margin than 100-day plans because of discounting and peak-load contractors. We agreed a margin target for DD, a revenue scenario to reach the 50% post-deal mix from Week 1, and left a DD price rise pending.

discussion.keyPoints: Simon's figures showed DD at 38% gross margin and 100-day plans at 52%. Contractors brought in for DD peaks cost about 1,100 GBP a day.
Average utilisation across 28 consultants was 68%, with DD leads swinging between 40% and over 100%.
Priya argued DD is underpriced for the risk it carries. Simon was nervous about losing panel places.

recommendations.recommendation: Lift DD gross margin from 38% to 45% by reducing peak contractor days by half.
Raise the standard DD fee from 35,000 GBP to 40,000 GBP for deals above 100m GBP enterprise value.
Model the base case on 18 delivery assurance retainers and 25 100-day plans next year to reach a 50% post-deal mix.
Measure lifetime value at fund level over 3 years, not per DD engagement.
Allocate a 60,000 GBP annual marketing budget tied to the Tech Risk Index and conference sponsorship.

actions.action: Build the service line margin model into the monthly board pack

nextFocus: Review progress on DD margin and post-deal mix at the first quarterly check-in.
nextPreparation: Priya to report DD-to-100-day plan conversion and retainer count.
